writeup.headline: Agilent rates Hold: strong momentum and solid quality offset by a valuation that is high on every measure.
writeup.thesis: Agilent scores 56, a Hold, because a very strong price trend (score 94) and good quality (score 71) are balanced by a weak valuation score of 16. The shares sit at their 52-week high, 33.7% above their 200-day average and 54.5 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. The business itself is sound: a 22.2% operating margin, a diluted share count down 0.7% year on year, and a balance sheet scoring 63. However, growth is middling (score 47), with TTM revenue growth of 8.6% and growth that slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation is high in absolute terms, at 6.9x sales, 32.6x EV/EBIT and 65.7x FCF excluding prepayments, and it is expensive against its own history, with P/S more expensive than at 56 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: Valuation is high in absolute terms, with the FCF yield 3.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, leaving little room for disappointment.
Revenue growth slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter, so the momentum in the shares may be running ahead of the business.
Reported cash flow is flattered by customer prepayments: contract liabilities rose $557.0M, and the FCF margin is 10.6% excluding them versus a reported 17.2%.
After a sharp run to its 52-week high, the stock is exposed to a pullback if the Q4 results in November fall short of the raised FY2026 outlook.
Tariff and trade exposure remains a standing risk, and the reported Proscia acquisition adds integration risk.
what_would_change: An upgrade to Buy needs 9 more points, most plausibly from growth re-accelerating or from the valuation score improving if the price eases or earnings catch up.
A downgrade to Sell would take a 12-point drop, for example if the trend score fades from 94 as momentum breaks while valuation stays weak.
Q4 results and FY2027 guidance in November could move the growth and news scores in either direction.
Weaker free cash flow once prepayments normalise would hurt the quality and valuation scores.
